events.title: The death of Queen Isabella of Castile
events.shortBlurb: The queen who completed the Reconquista and sent Columbus westward died at Medina del Campo, and an age of Spanish glory and shadow was set…
body: Isabella I of Castile, born on 22 April 1451 at Madrigal de las Altas Torres, joined her crown to that of Ferdinand of Aragon and so laid the foundation of a united Spain. In 1492 the two sovereigns took Granada, the last Moorish kingdom, ending the long Reconquista, and in that same year sponsored the voyage of Christopher Columbus across the ocean.

A queen of fervent and practical piety, she promoted the reform of the Spanish Church and its religious orders, aided by Cardinal Cisneros. Yet her reign is remembered also for its shadows, told here without gloss: the establishment of the Spanish Inquisition in 1478 and the expulsion of the Jews from her realms in 1492.

Worn by the deaths of her only son John and her daughter Isabella, she withdrew from the cares of government in September 1504. She died a little before noon on 26 November 1504 in the castle of La Mota at Medina del Campo, and was buried, by her own wish, at Granada. A cause for her beatification was in time opened, and she is styled a Servant of God.
